prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1227; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A dated repair quote from before the policy start shows this same damage already existed.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a left-turn collision at an intersection, in which an oncoming car struck the policyholder's vehicle as it turned. The claimant is represented by counsel, so all contact will go through that office.

Entry 2: Spoke with the household driver, who confirms the vehicle was turning left when the other car came through the junction. Police attended the scene and recorded the claimant as being in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 3: The other driver's account matches the policyholder's description of how the impact happened. Witnesses and scene photographs are consistent with that same sequence.

Entry 4: Claimant reports neck and back strain. The injury pattern described fits well with the kind and force expected from a side-on impact of this type.

Entry 5: The claimant has added some smaller details in later calls, but the core account has stayed the same. No earlier injury to the neck or back is known to us.

Entry 6: Treatment has followed a usual course, with visits tapering off as the claimant reported improvement. Counsel has asked for copies of the treatment records.

Entry 7: Inspection shows damage to the left side of the vehicle. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, but it is not yet clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.

Entry 8: A repair estimate that predates the policy start shows this same damage already existed. Referred to the claims supervisor for review before any further decision is made.

Entry 9: The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy. Coverage position remains under review pending resolution of the estimate question.
